messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: SRE on-call — High latency observed on continuous-batching path in prod us-west-2. p99 > 1.5s for last 5m, p95 ~ 400ms. Possible streaming stalls. Ticket: INC-27911
amanda: seeing it. dashboards show a p99 spike starting ~03:12 UTC. Streaming requests show stalls around batch size 8-16. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/contbatch
michael: I can join. Any customer-facing errors? logs show no 5xx, just long tails. :thinking_face:
rachel: customer-impact: a handful of high-QPS customers seeing slow responses (chat UX lag). CS pinged already.
amanda: stack: continuous-batcher -> runtime scheduler -> kv-cache. Recent rollout of scheduler fairness patch landed ~2h ago.
ben: I think mixed sequence lengths are amplifying padding. p99 spike correlates with more long-seqlen traffic.
amanda: agree. median seq len steady, but tail seq len (95/99) increased ~2x. amplifies per-batch runtime.
michael: can we get batch size percentiles? query: metrics.batch_size.percentiles{path="contbatch"}
amanda: ran it: 25%:2, 50%:4, 75%:8, 95%:16, 99%:24 — lots of mixed batches.
jen: the fairness change introduced linger_ms=6ms. That can clump short+long into same batch; a long request forces whole batch to run long seqlen.
amanda: immediate mitigations proposal:
- reduce linger_ms 6->2 in us-west-2 pools
- add routing rule: streaming-critical routes bypass continuous-batch and use streaming-only path
- targeted kv-evict in contbatch namespace
- consider shedding contbatch for specific heavy customers
michael: priority: reduce latency now -> reduce linger + routing shed.
jen: I can set linger_ms via control-plane flag. applying to usw2-contbatch pools now.
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: linger_ms set to 2 on 12 nodes in us-west-2 by jen at 03:30 UTC
ben: early telemetry: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 260ms in 2m, p99 trending down but still elevated.
rachel: CS update: alerted impacted customers, they reported improvement already to the web chat team.
amanda: next: add routing-policy rule for streaming routes and high-qps customers. michael, can you push a temporary rule?
michael: pushed rule to staging and rolled to prod at 03:38 UTC. rule: if route.type=="streaming" && customer in high-qps-set then prefer streaming-path.
ben: after routing change, p99 for streaming routes dropped near baseline for most; a few edge customers still heavy.
jen: batch compositions changed: fewer long+short mixes. KV-cache pressure unchanged.
amanda: residual p99 bump at ~03:46, possibly backlog from previously queued large batches.
jen: suggestion: targeted kv-evict on contbatch namespace to drop long-lived entries slowing lookups.
michael: caution — aggressive evict can increase cold-start tokenization.
amanda: agreed. do targeted eviction with rate-limit. ben?
ben: running:
```
./kv-evict --namespace contbatch --rate 50/s --dry-run=false
```
ben: started eviction at 03:49 UTC.
incident-bot: OP: kv-evict started by ben at 03:49 UTC against contbatch namespace
ben: tail CPU on workers improving, p99 down further.
rachel: CS update sent: mitigation in progress; expected improvement within 15m. customers appreciated prompt updates.
amanda: follow-ups to add to playbook: auto-shed policy when mixed-seqlen ratio > 0.25; scheduler should prefer homogenous batches.
jen: long-term: propose seq-length bucketing or separate batchers per seq-length class. will draft RFC.
michael: I'll keep watch for 30m then hand to rachel. page me on regressions.
amanda: handoff notes:
- root cause: mixed-seqlen amplification after fairness linger change
- mitigations: linger_ms reduced 6->2 (us-west-2), routing-policy to streaming-only for high-qps, targeted kv-evict
- status: p95/p99 improving, residual tail slightly above SLO for small subset
- follow-ups: scheduler homogeneity PR, auto-shed policy, playbook update
amanda: handing to rachel for next watch; will DM follow-up items and paste playbook.
rachel: ACK. taking the watch, coordinating with eng-runtime on RFC.
incident-bot: MONITORING: auto-check p95/p99 window stable for 10m; incident marked monitoring. Re-open INC-27911 if regress.
amanda: closing active page; keep monitoring. :white_check_mark:
michael: sample trace for postmortem:
```
# trace sample
batch_id=0x9f21 seqlen=2048 batch_size=12 runtime_ms=1420 scheduler_linger=6ms
```
ben: adding metrics links and timeline to INC-27911; will draft postmortem.
jen: starting scheduler-change RFC and tagging @product for throughput/cost tradeoffs.
amanda: thanks everyone. handoff complete.
rachel: monitoring window started at 03:55 UTC.
